Question_Text: Where do you live in Edmonton?
Option_Label: Enter Postal Code (e.g. T5J 2R7), Neighbourhood, or Street Address
Option_Hint: Identifies your neighbourhood street typology (Mature Laned, Infill & Duplex, Suburban Front Driveway, or Modern Townhome) to calibrate live curbside stall capacity.
Gains_Benefits: Customizes the visual street simulation to match the exact parking dynamics of your neighbourhood (garage lanes, curb cuts, density).
Pains_Costs: Requires entering postal code or address (protected under Section 4(c) of POPA).
Policy_Rationale: Customizes visual street simulations to match the exact parking dynamics of the respondent's neighbourhood

Question_Text: Where do you live in Edmonton?
Option_Label: Prefer not to share location (Opt Out)
Option_Hint: Skips location detection and loads Edmonton standard Mature Laned benchmark street.
Gains_Benefits: 100% anonymous survey participation without disclosing any geographical or postal information.
Pains_Costs: Simulation uses the city-wide benchmark rather than your specific neighbourhood street layout.
Policy_Rationale: Enables anonymous survey participation without disclosing geographical or postal information

Question_Text: Residential parking programs cost money to operate. Who should pay for them?
Option_Label: People who use parking through pay-per-use fees and parking permits.
Option_Hint: Drivers who park on the street pay permit fees. This covers program costs and encourages people with driveways to park off the street.
Gains_Benefits: Costs are covered by people using the program, rather than through property taxes.
Pains_Costs: Fees add to users’ parking costs, including for people with no private parking.
Policy_Rationale: Ensures program operating costs are paid directly by users rather than through property taxes

Question_Text: Residential parking programs cost money to operate. Who should pay for them?
Option_Hint: Because street parking is free, more vehicles park on the street.
Gains_Benefits: People can use the program without paying separate parking fees, reducing the direct cost of access.
Pains_Costs: Program costs are shared through property taxes, including by people who do not use the parking.
Policy_Rationale: Reduces direct costs to users by funding the program through property taxes instead of separate fees

Question_Text: In neighbourhoods where street parking is in high demand, should there be a limit on parking permits per household?
Option_Hint: Homes can only get permits for up to two street-parked cars. Extra vehicles must park in private driveways or garages.
Gains_Benefits: Limiting permits can reduce competition for street parking, improving availability for other residents and visitors
Pains_Costs: Households with more vehicles than permits would need other parking arrangements, which may be difficult if they have limited or no private parking
Policy_Rationale: Reduces competition for street parking to improve availability for other residents and visitors

Question_Text: In neighbourhoods where street parking is in high demand, should there be a limit on parking permits per household?
Option_Hint: Homes can get permits for 3 or more vehicles, so more cars end up parked along the curb.
Gains_Benefits: Households can obtain permits for all eligible vehicles, accommodating households with multiple drivers.
Pains_Costs: More vehicles may compete for the same spaces, making parking near home harder to find.
Policy_Rationale: Accommodates households with multiple drivers by allowing permits for all eligible vehicles

Question_Text: When street parking is in high demand, should visitors and service providers (e.g., cleaners and contractors) have the same opportunity as residents to park on the block they are visiting?
Option_Hint: Allows visitors, family, and service providers equal access to park near the home they are visiting.
Gains_Benefits: Family, friends and people providing services can use available spaces close to the home they’re visiting.
Pains_Costs: Residents face more competition for those spaces and may need to park farther from home.
Policy_Rationale: Allows family, friends, and service providers to park conveniently close to the homes they visit

Question_Text: When street parking is in high demand, should visitors and service providers (e.g., cleaners and contractors) have the same opportunity as residents to park on the block they are visiting?
Option_Hint: Prioritizes street parking for residents, reducing competition from visitor and service vehicles.
Gains_Benefits: Residents have priority for nearby spaces, reducing competition from visitor vehicles.
Pains_Costs: Visitors and service providers may need to park farther away, making visits less convenient.
Policy_Rationale: Prioritizes residents for nearby spaces by reducing competition from visitor vehicles

Question_Text: When people visit hospitals, post-secondary institutions and event venues, should they be able to use nearby residential streets for parking (within a few blocks)?
Option_Hint: Expands parking choices on nearby residential streets for patients, students, and event attendees.
Gains_Benefits: Patients, visitors, students and event attendees have more parking options within a few blocks of their destination.
Pains_Costs: Residents and their guests may face more competition for spaces and need to park farther away.
Policy_Rationale: Expands parking options for patients, students, visitors, and event attendees near major destinations

Question_Text: When people visit hospitals, post-secondary institutions and event venues, should they be able to use nearby residential streets for parking (within a few blocks)?
Option_Hint: Protects nearby residential street parking for residents and guests near major destinations.
Gains_Benefits: Residents and their guests face less competition for nearby spaces from people visiting these destinations.
Pains_Costs: People visiting nearby destinations have fewer street parking options and may need to park farther away, or use other parking facilities
Policy_Rationale: Protects residential street parking from institutional and event venue visitor spillover

Question_Text: When parking on the street near your home, what would you consider reasonably close?
Option_Hint: Limits acceptable parking to your immediate block to keep vehicles within a short walking distance.
Gains_Benefits: A short distance between your vehicle and home
Pains_Costs: Fewer spaces meet your preferences and your block may be full even when parking is available nearby.
Policy_Rationale: Limits acceptable parking distance to the immediate block to keep vehicles close to home

Question_Text: When parking on the street near your home, what would you consider reasonably close?
Option_Label: More possible spaces fall within the distance you consider acceptable.
Option_Hint: Increases available parking options by extending acceptable parking distance into the wider neighbourhood.
Gains_Benefits: More possible spaces fall within the distance you consider acceptable.
Pains_Costs: You may have a longer walk between your vehicle and home.
Policy_Rationale: Expands acceptable parking distance to the wider neighbourhood to increase available parking options

Question_Text: Should access to private parking affect who can get a permit? Consider all households, including those in houses, townhomes and apartments. Private parking means a driveway, garage or other off-street parking space.
Option_Label: Yes households with no private parking should get priority for permits
Option_Hint: Prioritizes street parking permits for households with fewer off-street parking alternatives.
Gains_Benefits: Prioritizes households with fewer alternatives to street parking, regardless of housing type.
Pains_Costs: Households with private parking may have less access to permits, even when the parking does not meet all their needs.
Policy_Rationale: Prioritizes street parking permits for households with no private off-street parking options

Question_Text: Should access to private parking affect who can get a permit? Consider all households, including those in houses, townhomes and apartments. Private parking means a driveway, garage or other off-street parking space.
Option_Label: No, households should have the same eligibility, whether or not they have private parking.
Option_Hint: Ensures equal permit eligibility for all households regardless of their private parking arrangements.
Gains_Benefits: Households have the same opportunity to obtain permits, regardless of their private parking arrangements
Pains_Costs: Households without private parking receive no additional priority and may face more competition for limited permits
Policy_Rationale: Ensures equal permit eligibility for all households regardless of private parking availability
